The telling is over: he sits back on the raised platform with his hands loosely folded together in his lap, eyes half-closed, a small satisfied smile. Ramu is a boy of about eleven with cropped black hair, a blue half-sleeve school shirt, khaki shorts and a cloth school bag. He sits on the ground leaning against the platform right beside the old man's knee, chin on his folded arms, wide awake. Four other children between seven and twelve are with them, in plain cotton frocks and shirts, barefoot.
